scope: Reference images and six sampled frames at0/1/2/3/4/5.125 seconds per video; not continuous audiovisual listening, beat scoring or new user ratings

assessment.staircase: All original/swapped/zero configurations retain small arm gestures and rear leg curls. The light-yellow top and grey trousers still become white/blue sportswear, often with a bag. B original and swapped share the same main motif; zero changes some positions and poses.
assessment.red_outfit: Most configurations retain hand-to-mouth, hand behind head and small upper-body gestures. A swapped and C zero show larger late two-arm movement; larger movement is not evidence of correct music-conditioned choreography, particularly when present in zero input.
assessment.shop: Mostly stationary single-arm gestures and small weight shifts across all three models and zero inputs. Local differences remain, but the sampled sequences do not demonstrate substantially different song-driven dance plans.
assessment.visual_quality: No obvious catastrophic frame corruption in inspected samples. No quantitative sharpness equivalence or full continuous visual-quality verdict is claimed.

evidence_boundaries: All300 models completed training and complete deployment/layout audits; the updated dense backbone was actually used.
Correct/wrong music representation diagnostics remain weak and train positional-mean H still has lower validation MSE.
Prediction-length changes also change packed layout; RGB differences do not isolate semantic control.
Length gradients were larger than semantic-loss gradients in four selected samples, but the length0.01 ablation did not establish a useful generation gain or a sole root cause.
One hundred and three hundred updates are bounded budget checks, not evidence of full convergence or impossibility of the overall music-to-H idea.
No DiT/video/denoising-prediction loss was introduced. Further generation-behavior supervision requires separate authorization.
